record.original_question: Describe all two-orbit polytopes of full rank.

evidence.quote: Problem 23. Describe all two-orbit polytopes of full rank.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set (with a least and a greatest face) satisfying the standard diamond condition and strong flag-connectedness, so that every flag (maximal chain) has exactly n+1 proper faces and, for each flag Φ and each i ∈ {0,1,…,n−1}, there is a unique flag Φ^i differing from Φ only in its rank-i face. The automorphism group Γ(P) acts freely on flags; P is called a two-orbit polytope if Γ(P) has exactly two orbits on the set of flags.

A geometric realization of an abstract polytope P of rank n is a (faithful) embedding of its faces into Euclidean space E^d (or, in the case of an apeirotope, a discrete one) such that Γ(P) is induced by Euclidean isometries. Such a realization is said to be of full rank when:
 (i) for a finite polytope, the affine hull of the realization has dimension equal to the rank n; 
 (ii) for an infinite polytope (apeirotope), the affine hull has dimension equal to n − 1.

Problem. Give a complete description (classification) of all two-orbit polytopes admitting a faithful geometric realization of full rank, in every rank n ≥ 3, listing for each rank the polytopes that occur, the class (among the 2^n − 1 possible two-orbit classes indexed by proper non-empty subsets I ⊊ {0,…,n−1}) to which each belongs, and their symmetry groups.
artifact.status_search_result: Regular polytopes of full rank were classified by McMullen, and chiral (and more generally two-orbit) polytopes have since received considerable structural study, including a 2026 manuscript developing a general structural theory of two-orbit polytopes of arbitrary rank with the 2^n−1 class decomposition. However, no source found provides a complete classification of two-orbit polytopes of full rank; the problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Two-Orbit Polytopes (arXiv:2604.00185)
status_evidence.snippet: Develops a general structural theory of two-orbit polytopes of arbitrary rank, classifying them into 2^n-1 classes by local flag configuration; foundational rather than enumerative.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work develops structural theory but does not provide a complete classification of two-orbit polytopes of full rank.

status_evidence.title: Regular Polytopes of Full Rank
status_evidence.snippet: Classifies regular polytopes of full rank in Euclidean spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The full-rank classification is known in the regular case (McMullen), motivating the analogous open question for two-orbit polytopes.

status_evidence.title: Polytope of full rank - Polytope Wiki
status_evidence.snippet: Defines polytope of full rank: finite non-degenerate polytope with dimension equal to rank, or apeirotope with dimension one less than rank.
status_evidence.claim: Standard definition of full rank used in the problem statement.
